# Norman Douglas

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v4 c28 P8](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0008), [v5 c15 P27](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0027), [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** old pagan  <sub>[v5 c16 P37](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0037)</sub>; ogre  <sub>[v5 c16 P49](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0049), [v5 c16 P60](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0060)</sub>

## Appearance

Norman Douglas is a fine-looking, big-framed man with a high, white, unwrinkled forehead and a sweep of long red beard over his broad chest. He possesses a mane of red hair, ungrizzled by age, and blue eyes that can flash with fire. In his youth, he was known as a handsome, red-haired young giant.

_Sources: [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c32 P2](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0002)_

## Personality

Norman Douglas is a boisterous, fiery-tempered man who is famous for his loud, booming voice, roaring laughter, and intense outbursts. Though he can be a bully when faced with timid or fearful people, he greatly respects women and individuals who show "spunk" and stand up to him. He is clever, well-read, outspoken, and generous, showing no hesitation to admit his mistakes or apologize when he realizes he was wrong.

_Sources: [v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028), [v5 c16 P29](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0029), [v5 c16 P30](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0030), [v5 c16 P54](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0054), [v5 c16 P55](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0055), [v5 c16 P59](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0059), [v5 c16 P79](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0079), [v5 c26 P19](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0019), [v5 c26 P21](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0021)_

## History

In his youth, Norman Douglas courted Ellen West for two years before a sudden quarrel caused them to break off their relationship. In a fit of temper, Norman hastily married Hester Reese, whom he came to despise due to her meekness and lack of spirit. After declaring that a session member had cheated him in a cow transaction, Norman refused to attend church for twenty years, though he allowed his late wife to go. When Faith Meredith visited his home to ask him to return to church and contribute to the salary, Norman initially intimidated and insulted her until she returned in a fiery rage to rebuke him; admiring her spirit, he struck a deal to contribute a hundred dollars a year and attend church once a month. His return to church caused a major stir in Glen St. Mary, and upon seeing Ellen West there after twenty years, he fell in love with her again. He began actively courting Ellen and eventually gained her consent after persuading her sister, Rosemary, to release Ellen from a long-standing promise. Norman expressed immense delight and satisfaction when his marriage to Ellen was settled.

_Sources: [v5 c15 P27](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0027), [v5 c15 P29](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0029), [v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c16 P30](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0030), [v5 c16 P39](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0039), [v5 c16 P50](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0050), [v5 c16 P55](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0055), [v5 c16 P59](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0059), [v5 c17 P0](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0000), [v5 c26 P17](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0017), [v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012), [v5 c32 P24](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0024), [v5 c35 P7](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0007)_

## Quotes

> Give me a spunky woman—spunk for me every time.  <sub>[v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031)</sub>

> I vow you’ve got spunk, after all—I like spunk. Come, sit down—sit down!  <sub>[v5 c16 P55](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0055)</sub>

> Look-a-here, girl, if you’ll shake hands and break bread with me I’ll pay what I used to to the salary and I’ll go to church the first Sunday in every month and I’ll make Kitty Alec hold her jaw.  <sub>[v5 c16 P59](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0059)</sub>

> She wasn’t very well just before I buried her ten years ago, but I reckon she has better health now  <sub>[v5 c17 P1](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0001)</sub>

> Look here, girl, Ellen and I want to marry each other. That’s plain English, isn’t it? Got that?  <sub>[v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012)</sub>
